author: Collected from the shepherds of the high moor
pages:
#The Light on the Moor

On winter nights, the shepherds say, you can sometimes see a small yellow light moving slowly across Frostmoor, swinging gently, as if carried by someone walking. If you follow it, it stays always a little ahead of you.

Most sensible folk do not follow it. This is the story of one who did.

#Ylva

Ylva was a shepherd girl whose youngest lamb had wandered off into a snowstorm. She went out after it with no lantern of her own, and soon she was lost, the snow so thick she could not see her own hands.

Then she saw the light: small, yellow, swinging. She ran towards it, and it moved away. She followed it for what felt like hours, stumbling through drifts, until at last it stopped.

#The Hollow

The light hung above a little hollow sheltered from the wind. In the hollow, curled up and shivering, was her lamb. And beside the lamb, half buried in the snow, was an old iron lantern, its glass cracked, its candle long burned out.

Ylva picked up the lamb, and the light went out.

#The Shepherd Who Did Not Come Home

The next spring, when the snow melted, the villagers found the remains of an old shepherd in that same hollow, still holding a crook. No one knew who he was. The oldest woman in the village said that, when she was a little girl, a shepherd had gone out into a storm after a lost lamb and never returned.

Ylva hung the old lantern above her door. On stormy nights she lights it, so that anyone lost on the moor can find their way home.
